title: Noetherian closed families have a finite universal intersection inside an open
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $v:V\hookrightarrow S$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $(\mathcal I_\lambda)_{\lambda\in L}$ be a family, indexed by a set $L$, of quasi-coherent ideal sheaves of $\mathcal O_V$ [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $C_\lambda\hookrightarrow V$ for the closed subscheme defined by $\mathcal I_\lambda$, in the sense that its ideal sheaf is $\mathcal I_\lambda$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. The sheaf sum $\mathcal I=\sum_{\lambda\in L}\mathcal I_\lambda$ is quasi-coherent; for every affine open $A=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq V$ it satisfies $\mathcal I|_A=\widetilde{\sum_{\lambda\in L}\mathcal I_\lambda(A)}$. There is a finite subset $L_0\subseteq L$ with $\mathcal I=\sum_{\lambda\in L_0}\mathcal I_\lambda$. If $L=\{d\in\mathbf N:d\geq m\}$, one may choose $N\geq m$ with $\mathcal I=\sum_{m\leq d\leq N}\mathcal I_d$, including $N=m$ when the sum is zero. There is a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ cut out by $\mathcal I$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], whose inverse image over $A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/\sum_\lambda\mathcal I_\lambda(A))$. For every scheme $T$ and map $t:T\to V$, $t$ factors uniquely through $Z$ if and only if it factors through every $C_\lambda$; equivalently, on affine charts of $T$ mapping into $A$, the induced ring maps annihilate every $\mathcal I_\lambda(A)$. The composite $v\circ i:Z\to S$ is an immersion of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. More precisely, for every affine open $B=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, there are finitely many $f_j\in R$ with $V\cap B=\bigcup_jD(f_j)$, and $Z\times_SB$ is covered by the affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(R_{f_j}/\mathcal I(D(f_j)))$. The statements allow empty $L$, empty $V$, and arbitrary, possibly non-Noetherian or nonreduced, test schemes $T$.

source.place: Bourbaki Expose 221, proof of Lemma 3.4 after Lemma 3.6, printed p.264, stationary intersections of closed subschemes; explicit ideal-sum and affine finite-type expansion by the agent. proof.text: First construct finite principal charts for the open. For any affine $B=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, $R$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Write the closed complement $B\setminus V$ as $V(K)$ for an ideal $K\subseteq R$, using the definition of the Zariski topology. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ of $K$. Then $V\cap B=\bigcup_{j=1}^r D(f_j)$: a prime fails to contain $K$ exactly when it misses a generator. These opens are affine with coordinate rings $R_{f_j}$ by clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme]. Quasi-compactness of $S$ gives a finite affine cover of $S$; applying this construction to its members gives a finite affine cover $(A_a)_{a\in E}$ of $V$. Each $\mathcal O_V(A_a)$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], applied to this affine open of $S$. Empty covers are allowed.

source.place: Tags 01OV (definition-noetherian) and 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian); schemes.tex Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine). The finite principal cover is the displayed elementary ideal argument.

proof.text: For every affine open $A\subseteq V$, put $J_A=\sum_{\lambda\in L}\mathcal I_\lambda(A)\subseteq\mathcal O_V(A)$. The affine section base-change statement [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change], together with the localization in clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme], says that $\mathcal I_\lambda(A_f)$ is the ideal generated by the restrictions of $\mathcal I_\lambda(A)$. Hence $J_{A_f}$ is generated by the restrictions of $J_A$: both ideals consist of finite sums of multiples of restrictions of elements of the individual $\mathcal I_\lambda(A)$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme] therefore constructs a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ with ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$ satisfying $\mathcal J(A)=J_A$ and $i^{-1}(A)=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_V(A)/J_A)$ over $A$. By [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent and $\mathcal J|_A=\widetilde{J_A}$.

source.place: Tag 01QQ (lemma-closed-immersion-bijection-ideals), affine compatible-ideal formulation; schemes.tex Tags 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme), 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine).

proof.text: The sheaf sum $\mathcal I$ is, by definition, the smallest sub-$\mathcal O_V$-module of $\mathcal O_V$ containing all the $\mathcal I_\lambda$. Each $\mathcal I_\lambda$ is contained in $\mathcal J$, as can be checked on sections of affine opens, so $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal J$. Conversely, for every affine $A$, every element of $\mathcal J(A)=J_A$ is a finite sum of elements of the ideals $\mathcal I_\lambda(A)$, hence belongs to $\mathcal I(A)$. These inclusions on an affine open basis give $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal I$. Thus $\mathcal I=\mathcal J$, proving quasi-coherence, the affine formula and the stated construction of $Z$. This construction and identification also apply to every subfamily, including the empty one.

source.place: Tag 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme); identification by the defining least-submodule property of the sheaf sum, following the compatible-ideal construction in step 2.

proof.text: On each of the finitely many $A_a$ from step 1, the ideal $J_{A_a}$ has a finite set of generators, since its section ring is Noetherian [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Express each generator as a finite sum of elements from the ideals $\mathcal I_\lambda(A_a)$ and collect their finitely many indices into $L_a$. Put $L_0=\bigcup_{a\in E}L_a$. Then $J_{A_a}=\sum_{\lambda\in L_0}\mathcal I_\lambda(A_a)$ for every $a$, since the right side is contained in $J_{A_a}$ and contains its generators. The construction in steps 2--3 for the subfamily $L_0$ identifies its ideal sheaf with $\mathcal I$ on this affine cover (and on its principal refinements by localization); hence the sheaves are equal. If $V$ or $L$ is empty, take $L_0=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 01Y8 (lemma-acc-coherent), finite-affine-cover proof; finite-generator argument for arbitrary set-indexed sums written out here rather than reducing only sequences.

proof.text: For the tail-indexed family choose $N=\max(\{m\}\cup L_0)$. Then $L_0\subseteq\{m,\ldots,N\}\subseteq L$, so the sum over that interval contains the sum over $L_0$, which is $\mathcal I$, and is contained in $\mathcal I$. It is therefore equal to $\mathcal I$. If $\mathcal I=0$, every $\mathcal I_d$ is zero because it is a subideal of the sum, so $N=m$ works.

source.place: Tag 01Y8 (lemma-acc-coherent); elementary finite-maximum consequence of step 4.

proof.text: For any $t:T\to V$, factorization through $i$ implies annihilation of $\mathcal I(A)$ on every affine $A\subseteq V$, by its kernel description [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Conversely, such annihilation gives a factorization through $i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-lift-ideal-kills-sections]. The same two implications hold for each $C_\lambda$. Since $\mathcal I(A)=\sum_\lambda\mathcal I_\lambda(A)$, annihilating $\mathcal I(A)$ is equivalent to annihilating every summand. Thus $t$ factors through $Z$ exactly when it factors through every $C_\lambda$. Uniqueness follows because $i$ is a monomorphism, as stated in [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-closed-finite-presentation], applied to $S$, its open $V$, and the constructed closed $Z$. Finally vanishing in $\mathcal O_T(t^{-1}A)$ is equivalent to vanishing after restriction to every affine chart $W\subseteq t^{-1}A$, by the separatedness axiom for the structure sheaf. On such a chart it says exactly that $\mathcal O_V(A)\to\mathcal O_T(W)$ annihilates the indicated ideals. This proves the affine-test formulation without any Noetherian or reducedness assumption on $T$.

source.place: Tag 01HP (lemma-characterize-closed-subspace); properties.tex Tag 01OW and the monomorphism assertion used from the existing Noetherian open-closed lemma.

proof.text: The factorization $Z\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{v}S$ is an immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For an arbitrary affine $B=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, use the finite principal cover from step 1. The inverse images of its members in $Z$ are, by step 2, $\operatorname{Spec}(R_{f_j}/\mathcal I(D(f_j)))$, and they cover $Z\times_S B$. Each displayed coordinate algebra is generated over $R$ by the image of $1/f_j$: every element is the image of a fraction $a/f_j^n$. Thus this is a finite affine cover by finitely generated $R$-algebras, proving finite type directly by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], as well as the more precise chart claim. If the open is empty the empty affine cover works. If $L=\varnothing$, all $J_A=0$, so the same quotient charts give $Z=V$ and the universal property is vacuous, as required.

source.place: Tags 01T0 (section-finite-type) and 01T2 (definition-finite-type); schemes.tex Tag 01IO (definition-immersion). The finite algebra generators and charts are explicit consequences of steps 1--2.
